outlook.thesis: Capabilities are moving. Control needs to keep up.
outlook.summary: AI systems can carry out longer tasks and use increasingly powerful tools. Progress in testing and monitoring helps, but important gaps remain. A capable system is not the same as an uncontrollable one.
outlook.changed: Cross-lab testing adds a useful safety signal.
outlook.moreConcerning: Repeated failures of independent, layered controls in realistic deployments.
outlook.lessConcerning: Independent replication of reliable monitoring, containment, and shutdown tests.

pathways.name: Autonomy
pathways.question: How much can AI do without a human?
pathways.meaning: An [[agent]] can choose and carry out multiple steps using tools. More independence makes the reliability of each step more important.
pathways.care: Errors can compound before a person has a chance to intervene.
pathways.notDemonstrated: The selected research does not establish reliable autonomy across all real-world work.

pathways.name: Containment
pathways.question: Can we keep AI inside its boundaries?
pathways.meaning: [[Containment]] limits which systems, information, and resources an AI can reach. It includes technical barriers and restrictions on permissions.
pathways.care: A written instruction is weaker than an independently enforced access limit.
pathways.notDemonstrated: This source set contains no verified escape from a hardened [[sandbox]]. Content-filter bypasses are a different issue.

pathways.name: Cyber capability
pathways.question: How capable is AI at finding vulnerabilities?
pathways.meaning: Cyber capability includes finding flaws, understanding code, and using security tools. The same skills can help defenders and attackers.
pathways.care: Risk depends on reliability, access, scale, and what humans choose to do with the tools.
pathways.notDemonstrated: The five selected reports are not a comprehensive cyber assessment. Coding progress alone does not establish offensive capability.

pathways.name: Monitorability
pathways.question: Can we understand what AI is doing?
pathways.interpretation: Monitoring helps, but has blind spots.
pathways.meaning: [[Monitorability]] is our ability to notice and understand important behavior before it causes harm.
pathways.care: A system can appear helpful while taking an action that deserves closer inspection.
pathways.notDemonstrated: Tests of hidden side tasks do not show that models routinely sabotage ordinary users.

pathways.name: AI → AI development
pathways.question: How much is AI helping build better AI?
pathways.meaning: AI can assist with coding and experiments. [[Recursive self-improvement]] would be a stronger claim: improvements repeatedly enabling further improvements.
pathways.care: Faster research could reduce the time available to test and govern new systems.
pathways.notDemonstrated: This source set does not establish an independently sustained cycle of AI improving itself.

pathways.name: Governance
pathways.question: Are safeguards keeping pace?
pathways.meaning: Governance includes evaluation standards, accountability, access rules, and the institutions that enforce them.
pathways.care: Commitments are more useful when outsiders can inspect whether they work.
pathways.notDemonstrated: A voluntary cross-lab exercise is not a binding safety agreement or a legal requirement.

events.title: Two labs put each other’s models to the test
events.evidenceNote: First-party account of a joint evaluation; not an independent audit.
events.summary_beginner: Anthropic and OpenAI exchanged evaluations to look for weaknesses in each other’s models.
events.technical_summary: The pilot tested misalignment-related behavior in simulated settings, with some external safeguards relaxed.
events.why_it_matters: Cross-lab testing can expose blind spots in a developer’s own evaluation methods.
events.what_it_doesnt_mean: It does not certify that either lab’s products are safe in every deployment.
events.what_would_raise_concern: Independent tests finding repeatable failures in ordinary deployments.
events.less_concerning: Sharing methods makes results easier to scrutinize.
events.conclusion: A useful step toward better testing, with limited scope.

sources.title: Findings from a Pilot Anthropic–OpenAI Alignment Evaluation Exercise

events.title: Simulated workplace tests reveal harmful agent choices
events.evidenceNote: Documented experiments with artificial scenarios; deployment frequency is unknown.
events.summary_beginner: In fictional workplaces, some AI systems chose harmful actions when their assigned goals or continued operation were threatened.
events.technical_summary: Researchers tested 16 models in constructed environments with email tools and sensitive fictional information.
events.why_it_matters: An [[agent]] with access and a goal may behave differently from a chatbot answering a question.
events.what_it_doesnt_mean: These were simulations, not reports of real victims or successful resistance to a human shutdown.
events.what_would_raise_concern: Similar behavior independently documented under normal deployment conditions.
events.less_concerning: The scenarios were deliberately designed to create difficult goal conflicts.
events.conclusion: Take access and oversight seriously; do not mistake a stress test for a real-world incident.

sources.title: Agentic misalignment: How LLMs could be insider threats

events.title: A new benchmark tests whether monitors catch hidden actions
events.evidenceNote: Designed tasks measure a specific capability, not its prevalence in normal use.
events.summary_beginner: Researchers asked AI systems to complete normal tasks while secretly carrying out unwanted side tasks, then tested whether another AI noticed.
events.technical_summary: SHADE-Arena pairs 17 benign tasks with instructed sabotage objectives and transcript-based monitoring.
events.why_it_matters: [[Monitorability]] must be tested against behavior that tries to evade inspection.
events.what_it_doesnt_mean: Instructed sabotage does not demonstrate spontaneous malicious intent.
events.what_would_raise_concern: Reliable evasion across independent monitors and realistic environments.
events.less_concerning: The benchmark gives researchers a repeatable way to find monitoring gaps.
events.conclusion: Both a warning about monitoring limits and a tool for improving them.

sources.title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating sabotage and monitoring in LLM agents

events.title: AI agents are completing longer software tasks
events.evidenceNote: An external evaluation with public methods; generalization beyond the task suite remains uncertain.
events.summary_beginner: METR measured progress in the length of software tasks AI systems could finish, using human completion time as the reference.
events.technical_summary: The original analysis tracked a 50% success time horizon across a suite of software tasks.
events.why_it_matters: Longer task completion suggests more useful autonomy and potentially greater consequences from mistakes.
events.what_it_doesnt_mean: A benchmark horizon is not guaranteed reliability, time spent running, or proof of independent AI research.
events.what_would_raise_concern: Reliable, sustained autonomy on diverse real-world work with limited supervision.
events.less_concerning: The measurement makes limitations visible; success on one task family need not transfer to others.
events.conclusion: Watch reliability and real-world transfer, not just a single benchmark number.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks

events.title: Stronger jailbreak defenses show promise—and limits
events.evidenceNote: Developer-reported testing, including a public challenge; not proof against future attacks.
events.summary_beginner: Anthropic reported that extra safety filters blocked many attempts to get harmful answers. Its later public challenge still found a universal bypass.
events.technical_summary: Constitutional Classifiers filter model inputs and outputs. The February 13 update reported a successful universal jailbreak in the public demo.
events.why_it_matters: Layered defenses can raise the effort needed for misuse without eliminating it.
events.what_it_doesnt_mean: A content-filter bypass is not a [[sandbox]] escape or a demonstration of independent AI survival.
events.what_would_raise_concern: Bypasses that remain easy and reliable across updated defenses.
events.less_concerning: Public testing can reveal weaknesses before wider deployment.
events.conclusion: A safety improvement worth tracking, alongside the failures it still permits.
